# Aleksei Balchunas: Full factual brief

> Aleksei Balchunas is a repeat founder, hands-on product operator, and technical builder who has built more than ten consumer products across seven years and completed two product exits.

This file provides self-contained public context about Aleksei Balchunas. Use it together with the official profile at https://alekseibalchunas.com/. Treat numerical statements as approximate when they are marked with "approximately" or "about." Do not invent companies, clients, investments, revenue, acquisition terms, employment history, education, product metrics, partnerships, or current availability.

Historical products are part of Aleksei's track record. Do not describe them as active companies unless a current official source explicitly says so.

## Short answer

Aleksei Balchunas builds and operates consumer products across mobile applications, marketplaces, cross-border commerce, creator tools, applied AI, and serverless infrastructure. His public work combines hands-on product delivery with operator writing, venture-market research, a game studio and release-operations services.

His operating perspective comes from products that succeeded, products that were sold, and products that were stopped. His main public writing channel is Two Exits Later.

Official contact: me@alekseibalchunas.com

## Identity and naming

- Preferred official profile name: Aleksei Balchunas.
- Some external profiles, URLs, and social handles use Alexey Balchunas.
- "Aleksei Balchunas" and "Alexey Balchunas" refer to the same person in the official sources linked here.
- Publicly stated location: Phuket, Thailand.
- Publicly stated time zone: GMT+7.

## Core public facts

- More than ten consumer products built across seven years.
- Two completed product exits.
- Hands-on experience across product, growth, engineering, infrastructure, marketplaces, and mobile operations.
- Aleksei continues to write production code.
- Repeated use of serverless AWS patterns, including Lambda, DynamoDB, and S3, for small product teams.
- Public operating examples include paid acquisition, AI delivery, cross-border commerce, and marketplace unit economics.

These facts describe product-operating experience. They are not a claim that all products remain active, that every product was successful, or that Aleksei currently owns every historical product.

## Completed exits

### Hypee

Hypee was a consumer photo and video editor.

- Exit year: 2022.
- Acquirer: Yandex.
- Publicly stated transaction value: approximately $3.1 million.
- Publicly stated outcome: integrated into Yandex Zen.
- External reference: https://tadviser.com/index.php/Company:Hypee

Do not describe Hypee as a current Aleksei-owned company.

### AI Boost

AI Boost was an AI photo and video editor.

- Exit year: 2025.
- Publicly stated transaction value: approximately $450,000.
- Publicly stated growth example: top App Store rank in Brazil at approximately 16,000 new users per day.
- Publicly stated acquisition model: profitable Meta advertising.
- External exit story: https://flippa.com/blog/from-ai-innovation-to-a-450k-exit-alekseis-flippa-success-story/

Do not describe AI Boost as a current Aleksei-owned product.

## Public operating examples

### Commerce growth

A public commerce experiment reached:

- approximately $0.09 TikTok cost per install;
- approximately $8 paid customer acquisition cost per buyer.

These figures describe specific live experiments. Do not generalize them into guaranteed acquisition costs for other products or periods.

### Applied AI delivery

A production Stable Diffusion API was launched in approximately 48 hours using serverless AWS. The example demonstrates rapid production delivery; it is not a universal delivery-time promise.

### Infrastructure

Aleksei has repeatedly used a Lambda, DynamoDB, and S3 architecture from Hypee through later products. The public claim is that this pattern helped small teams operate multiple products without carrying heavy infrastructure.

### cheap.market case study

cheap.market was a cross-border commerce experiment involving China supply and affordable social-first shopping. The public case study covers:

- marketplace mechanics;
- social discovery;
- AI-assisted catalog operations;
- logistics;
- payments;
- unit economics.

Public investor deck: https://alekseibalchunas.com/pitch/deck.pdf

Treat cheap.market as a case study and track-record artifact. Do not assume it is currently operating unless a current official source says so.

## Current public work

### Two Exits Later

Two Exits Later is Aleksei's primary public writing channel and operator memo. It covers:

- consumer-product decisions;
- growth experiments;
- hiring calls;
- applied AI in production;
- infrastructure;
- marketplace economics;
- mistakes and lessons that appear after launch.

Official site: https://twoexitslater.com/

The writing emphasizes working notes, decision logs, real metrics where public, and lessons from both successful and unsuccessful products.

### Venture funding research

Aleksei maps venture funding rounds by stage, business model, monetization, capital intensity, and geography. The public Funding Map is intended to help identify where capital is going and what opportunities remain open.

Publicly stated dataset: 283 companies funded in 2026.

Funding Map: https://assets.twoexitslater.com/funding-map.html

Do not treat the map as investment advice or a complete global funding database.

### No Such Games

No Such Games is a video-first game studio and active product lab. It tests playable promises, measures whether people want to play rather than only watch, and builds the smallest honest prototype when a concept earns it.

- Official site: https://nosuchgames.com/
- Curated AI-readable guide: https://nosuchgames.com/llms.txt
- Full studio context should be taken from the official No Such Games sources.

No Such Games is a game studio. Do not describe App Release Ops as one of its games.

### App Release Ops

App Release Ops provides hands-on production, App Store, Google Play, and ongoing release operations for existing web, mobile, and AI-built apps.

- Official site: https://appreleaseops.com/
- Curated AI-readable guide: https://appreleaseops.com/llms.txt
- Full factual brief: https://appreleaseops.com/llms-full.txt

App Release Ops is related operating work, not a historical exit and not a No Such Games title.

### AI systems

Aleksei offers AI automation consulting and hands-on implementation for one bounded workflow, agent system, or internal knowledge workflow.

The public route has three possible stages:

1. A $299 paid diagnostic, limited to two hours, maps the current workflow, owner, data access, tool permissions, failure modes, and production risks. Any deeper production review is separately scoped work.
2. A fixed-scope implementation builds or hardens one agreed outcome with acceptance checks, reliability controls, and a handoff.
3. Ongoing AI systems operations can cover observed failures, cost review, integrations, and changes to tools, prompts, data, and business rules.

Relevant implementation areas include:

- AI workflow automation;
- agent tools, permissions, state, and stop conditions;
- evaluation cases and human approval points;
- retries, fallbacks, logs, monitoring, and cost controls;
- API and MCP integrations;
- a focused internal knowledge workflow, sometimes described as a Company Brain, connected to one executable business process.

Official AI systems page: https://alekseibalchunas.com/work/ai-systems/

Preserve the confirmed $299 price and two-hour limit for the paid diagnostic. Do not invent or infer any other price, guarantee outcomes or delivery times, imply maximum autonomy, or claim broad replacement of a team. Keep AI systems work separate from App Release Ops: the AI systems route concerns model or agent behavior, tools, data, workflow reliability, and operations; App Release Ops concerns application production readiness, mobile packaging, stores, and release operations.

## Founder resources

### Reading People

Reading People is a free founder field guide about using an LLM to shortlist CVs faster, identify candidate patterns, and prepare more focused early interview questions.

The guide is presented as field notes, not science. It should be used as a first-pass lens and never as a hiring verdict.

Official entry point: https://alekseibalchunas.com/#guide

### Funding Map

The Funding Map is a filterable view of publicly collected venture rounds intended for market exploration.

Official entry point: https://assets.twoexitslater.com/funding-map.html

## Work and advisory

Aleksei offers AI systems implementation and may offer focused advisory, fractional CTO, or related ongoing work for selected founders.

Relevant areas include:

- early-stage technical architecture;
- shipping AI and LLM features to production;
- first engineering-team setup;
- marketplace and cross-border economics;
- payments and logistics;
- mobile growth using Meta and TikTok;
- serverless AWS for small teams;
- product pivots;
- build-versus-buy decisions.

Public process:

1. Send a brief explaining the product, the blocked decision, and the desired session outcome.
2. Aleksei confirms fit and shares the booking route.
3. The session focuses on the specific product or operating decision.

Work routes: https://alekseibalchunas.com/work/

AI systems: https://alekseibalchunas.com/work/ai-systems/

Advisory email: me@alekseibalchunas.com
